title: Session timeline Part 2: "Sessions on one clock" on the task page
description:
## As asked

Part 2 of **LIN-4395**: "A task shows the sessions that ran it, on one clock". This part is the picture. It is its own PR and is built on Part 1 (LIN-4404, the whole-life task cost read), which must land first.

**Where to read the parent.** Read LIN-4395's description: the `## As asked` block, `## Size of the move`, `## Design (chosen approach)` and `## Implementation Plan` (plan pass of 10 Nov at `b315e0e8f`, including "Departures from the design"). Then read the `### Plan Review Verdict` comment (Approve, comment `6ace09f6-de0d-45c1-a3e4-197be9aed902`) and its builder notes 5–9. Also read John's guest ruling, comment `31484e36-cefe-4053-9aed-2fb128ee3707`. **The parent's approved plan is where this piece starts.** Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4395.

**Done when** (the parent's line): "a person can open any task and see, in one picture on one clock, every session that ran it with its kind, model, time and cost, and when it merged (if it has); and it reads well on desktop and phone". The one ruled narrowing is that guests see the picture without dollars.

### Slice of the approved plan

**Files and approach**

* New `lib/session-roles.js`: `roleOf({ kind, followUpTo })` returns `wake`, then `resumed` (a non-wake with `followUpTo`), then `orchestration` (imported `ORCHESTRATION_KINDS`), then `work`, in that order. A lineage is **held** when its base is orchestration and it has wakes. It is **fresh** when its base is work. **Builder note 6:** a plain `custom` base with no wakes is neither held nor fresh, so label it by its kind. **Do not** switch Stages' `groupSessions` to this helper (Departure 1): resumed `custom` ci-wake rows would leave Stages' check-ins.
* New `lib/task-timeline.js`. It holds a pure `taskTimeline({ sessions, foundedElsewhere, merges, openItemIds, now })` that returns `{ lanes, scale, marks, totals }`, plus `withoutSpend(timeline)` and `createTaskTimelineReader(deps)`. The reader composes Part 1's `readTaskCost` (no app-call summary, with the `foundedElsewhere` opt-in), the close-out events and `taskTimeline`. Keep timeline logic out of the loader.
  * Lanes are ordered by start. An own lane runs from `dispatchedAt` to `dispatchedAt + durationMs`. A lane is running when one of its dispatch itemIds is an open session in the page model (`loopId === item.id`, `isOpenState` in `lib/task-state.js`), not when the worker row says so. A running lane extends to now. A lane that has no end and is not running stops at its last known request or dispatch and says "end not recorded".
  * Working segments are `[firstRequestAt, lastRequestAt]` per dispatch, with a minimum visible width. Held time is a thin line, and wakes and resumes get ticks. A dispatch with no records gets a tick, never a guessed bar. A lineage with `dispatches: null` gets its known span outlined as "working times unknown".
  * Long intervals with no work and no relevant marks fold into labelled breaks, and held lines still cross them. Start the threshold at 10 min or 15 % of the span and tune it against the LIN-4393 fixture.
  * Foreign-founded lanes (**builder note 7**) draw only this task's tagged dispatches. Clip their held line to this task's clock and mark the clipped ends "continues outside this task". Label their figure "lineage cost, counted under LIN-X" and leave it out of the total.
  * The total is the own read's `totalUsd`. When that is null, show "not complete" and name any priced part as priced. Truncation (Part 1's flag) also reads "not complete".
  * One merge rule: de-duplicate merged close-out events by `prUrl` and mark each recorded `prMergedAt`. If none is timed, use `pr.mergedAt` from `run-evidence`, on page load only. Otherwise show "merged, time not recorded" with no rule. Reusing the loader's events is allowed.
  * `withoutSpend` returns a **copy** and never mutates a cached model (builder note 5).
* `lib/run-evidence.js`: add `pr.mergedAt` from GitHub's `merged_at` (Departure 4; it is dropped at `run-evidence.js:80` today). The change is additive.
* New `lib/render-task-timeline.js`: positioned HTML, with no SVG and no layout maths in the browser. On desktop, a label column (kind · model · took / worked · cost) sits beside the track. Below 600 px, CSS alone puts labels above full-width tracks on the same clock. Each lane is a `<details>` listing its dispatches, with a fully named accessible `<summary>` (front-end-pages lesson, 8 Nov). Format dollars only through `formatUsd` and keep the renderer viewer-blind. Add `data-testid`, `data-role`, `data-kind` and `data-state`, and put no cost in any attribute.
* `lib/task-page-loader.js`: inject a new dep, `readTaskTimeline`. `loadTaskPage` sets `model.timeline`. `loadTaskState` never calls it, so the pinned `/state` keys stay unchanged and a quiet poll does no cost read. A read failure renders "sessions could not be read" and the page still loads.
* `lib/render-task-page.js`: add a "Sessions on one clock" section beneath Stages. Stages' markup is unchanged.
* Routes: `routes/task-page.js` adds `GET /workspace/:urlKey/api/task/:identifier/timeline` (owners and members). `routes/task-share.js` applies `withoutSpend` before rendering `/t/:token`, and adds `GET /t/:token/timeline`, which goes through `resolveScopedRecord` → the page's single-flight short cache (`cachedLoadPage`, `routes/task-share.js:119`, builder note 5) → `withoutSpend` → `maskFragment`. Both fragments get their open IDs from `loader.loadTaskState` (stored facts only). Polling and fragments make no GitHub calls. Wire the reader in `server.js`.
* `public/task-page.js`: fetch the fragment URL (from a data attribute on the section) when the poll's `trackHtml` changes, or every 60 s while a lane is `data-state="running"`. **Builder note 8:** update the comment at `public/task-page.js:71` ("Every request it makes is `fetchJson(stateUrl)`") and any test that pins it.
* Docs: add `session-roles` and `task-timeline` to runs-and-dispatch in `docs/areas/areas.json` (`render-task-timeline` belongs to front-end-pages by its prefix). Update `docs/architecture/source-map.md`, and document the new `data-*` attributes in `public/llms.txt`.

**Testing strategy**

* `session-roles` gives every kind in `DISPATCH_KINDS` and `ROW_ONLY_KINDS` a role (`leftover` reads as resumed), and the plain-`custom` case is labelled by kind.
* **LIN-4393 fixture**, taken from real `/cost` output plus request records: eight lanes; the autopilot about 63 min elapsed, about 6 min worked, five wake ticks; the implementation's `leftover` resume with two working segments; parallel surveys; a merge mark.
* Cases: late-posted request assignment, null timestamps, working times unknown, running (open end), missing end, a two-day gap folded into one labelled break with a held line crossing it, foreign-lane clipping, untimed merge, a truncated lineage reading "not complete", and `custom` roles.
* **Builder note 9:** render the task page itself for a task whose only lineage is 40 days old, and assert the section shows its sessions.
* **Guest test:** fetch all three guest responses for a priced task (`/t/:token`, `/t/:token/timeline`, `/t/:token/state`) and assert no `$` figure and no cost attribute in any of them. Assert that `withoutSpend` does not mutate the cached model.
* Stages' existing tests and the renderer golden are unchanged apart from the new section. Route tests cover both fragments.
* e2e at 390 px: no horizontal scroll, labels sit above tracks, and a lane's `<details>` opens to its dispatches.

**Acceptance**

* An owner or member opening any task, LIN-4393 and a 40-day-old task included, sees "Sessions on one clock". It shows every session with its kind, model, elapsed versus worked time and cost, wake and resume ticks, and the merge mark or the merge wording.
* Guests see the same picture with no dollars anywhere in the page, the fragment or state.
* It reads well at 390 px and on desktop. The `/state` keys are unchanged. Live Console, `timeline-zoom.js`, the run-page step model and `pipeline-churn` are untouched.

Session fit: fits one session

Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4395's approving plan-review (comment 6ace09f6-de0d-45c1-a3e4-197be9aed902, rev 1)

Grounding commit: `b315e0e8f3e1e5f3b5d6e634e53c5dc83b41d754`. Re-checked at breakdown (10 Nov) against origin/main `3b1b57b15`, with only wording changes to area notes since. Rebase onto Part 1's merge before starting.

**Constraints carried from the parent:** working time must never imply that elapsed or held time is work. Unknown timing and incomplete pricing stay visibly unknown or incomplete. Foreign-founded costs stay attributed to their founder, and their history must not stretch this task's clock. Any retiring or merging of existing views needs a separate ruling.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** Delivers the one-clock session picture on every task page, with guests shown no dollars; the earlier part already settled the whole-life read, and no survey finding is needed for the picture to work, so nothing larger binds.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Implemented

Implemented and merged in PR [#2390](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2390>) (merge `d9480093`, deployed 10 Nov). Every task page now has "Sessions on one clock" under Stages; guests see it without dollars. Built as the parent's approved plan, with the departures recorded on LIN-4395 (comment `d61b450d`) and accepted by review. Close-out added the done-edge final read, the guest pricing-words test and the runs-and-dispatch lesson. Follow-ups: LIN-3813 (linked), LIN-4409, LIN-4410. The full history is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4405 @ 9cf51ef72

**Ground.** Part 1 has landed (#2386, #2388), so nothing is blocked. The ticket targets the real thing, not a symptom. Its hard limit is data: request records began about 4 Nov, so older lineages come back with `dispatches: null`. That means builder note 9's 40-day witness only tests the "working times unknown" outline, and any task more than a week old shows outlines, not working bars. `LINEAGE_QUERY_LIMIT` is now `readTaskCost`'s default, so there's nothing to wire.

**Why it will be hard**

1. **The guest fragment's cache won't hold.** `cachedLoadPage` (`routes/task-share.js:119`) caches `loadTaskPage`, which reads the tracker and PR status (`lib/task-page-loader.js:1317-1337`). Its TTL is 5 s (`:51`) and the fragment polls every 60 s, so every guest poll misses and does a full page load. That breaks the plan's "fragments make no GitHub calls" and "open IDs from `loadTaskState`". The private fragment has no cache at all.
2. **Truncation is coarse and moves lanes.** `durationMs` starts at the earliest *fetched* member (`lib/cost-read.js:604-618`). When the newest-2,000 cap drops old rows, the lane's start shifts later without notice. `lineagesTruncated` is shared by every anchor, so one huge parent lineage pulled in by a single wake marks this task's own total "not complete". Use each lineage's own `incomplete` for its lane, and decide on purpose what the shared flag does to the total.
3. **Foreign lanes carry the parent's clock.** `sessionOf` gives a foreign lineage the parent's start, duration, model and every member's dispatches (`cost-read.js:471-475`). The scale and break pass must see only the `taggedItemIds` dispatches. LIN-4393 has no foreign lane, so only synthetic tests cover this.
4. **ci-wake rows label as "resumed".** They are `custom` + `followUpTo`, and `roleOf` checks resumed first. Choose the tick wording deliberately. The same choice decides whether a lineage driven only by CI wakes counts as "held".
5. **The `trackHtml` trigger is noisy.** A running chip shows its elapsed minutes (`lib/render-task-page.js:405-409`), so `trackHtml` changes about once a minute, which repeats the 60 s timer. Allow one fetch per window, and stop the new timer when the poller stops (done, or the tab is hidden).
6. **Size.** One session is tight: four new modules, six edited files, two routes, a second kind of browser request, guest and 390 px tests. The `/cost` wire strips `incomplete` and `lineagesTruncated`, so the LIN-4393 fixture must come from the in-process read.

**What I'd do first**

1. Give the timeline fragment its own single-flight cache, holding `loadTaskState`'s open IDs plus `readTaskTimeline`, with a TTL of at least the poll interval and shared by both routes. Post it on LIN-4395 as a departure from builder note 5.
2. Record the LIN-4393 fixture before writing `taskTimeline`. The break threshold and the "about 6 of 63 min" check can only be tuned against it.

## Survey global: LIN-4405 @ 9cf51ef72

**Where it lands.** Part 1 has landed (`lib/task-cost-read.js`, fa4bb76fb / d84b2b1db), so the read this builds on exists and is tested. The task page's loader grew from 746 to 1544 lines between 11 Oct and today. The renderer held at about 1015 lines because LIN-4103 took the estimates out. No dollars appear on the task page today (`render-task-page.js` doesn't import `formatUsd`), and the guest page is the owner page with its controls left out, behind `maskFragment`. This will be the first money on the page. It is also the first time the guest path must take something *out of the model* rather than leave a fragment out. The three-response guest test is what keeps that new gate honest.

**What the obvious way does**
- *Two reads of one history.* Page sessions come from `getLoopsForIssue`, one per dispatch and carrying state. Timeline lanes come from `readTaskCost`, one per lineage and carrying request records. They are joined by item id to decide "running". Every page load reads the task's dispatch rows twice by different routes. A row in one read but not the other draws inconsistently: a queued item, or a member dropped by truncation. This is the deeper thing: the page has two models of "a task's sessions". This ticket needn't close that seam, but it should test a loop with no lineage.
- *Two "took"s side by side.* A Stage's `durationMs` is the latest attempt's start to end (`toStage`, LIN-3498). A lane runs from the lineage base's `dispatchedAt` to its last completion (`cost-read.js:613`). For a retried stage or a `leftover` resume, these two numbers disagree a few inches apart. The labels must say which is which.
- *Another kind→role map.* Kinds are already classified in `run-view.js` `ORCHESTRATION_KINDS` (the loader takes it through `effort-readout.js`'s re-export), in `wall-clock-summary`'s buckets, and in a stale private copy at `pipeline-churn.js:55` that lacks `periodical`. `session-roles` should import from `run-view.js` and join the `ROW_ONLY_KINDS` census pattern (`wall-clock-summary.test`, `run-view-stages.test`).
- *Merge events.* `readMergedBy` already lists close-out events on every page load. If the reader re-reads them, that is a second read and a second dedup rule. Hand the loader's events in instead.
- *Inventories.* `areas.json` is test-pinned (`area-map-placement`), so a missed placement fails. Nothing I found checks `source-map.md`, the `llms.txt` data-attribute entries, or the `public/task-page.js:71` comment, so those would drift silently.
- *Load.* Owner routes are `no-store` with no cache. A running lane would re-run the whole cost read, request records included, every 60 s for each open tab. Only the guest side has `cachedLoadPage`.

**Better, and carryable:** import roles from `run-view.js`; pass the merge events in; give the two durations distinct words; give the owner fragment a short single-flight cache like the guest's; add one case where a loop has no lineage.

**Better still, not this task's:** one session model for the task page that Stages and the timeline both read; retiring `pipeline-churn`'s private `ORCHESTRATION_KINDS`; splitting the loader before the next dependency lands in it.

### Leftovers

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2390, head `719bc9e622f910dce4dfc658516ddccf2a85579c`. CI `ci-success` passed (unit tests, four E2E shards, secret scan).

- **Tidied.** `lib/render-task-timeline.js` had its own month table and UTC date format beside `fmtWhen`. It now uses `fmtWhen` (`lib/task-page-loader.js`).
- **Tidied.** The header of `routes/task-share.js` was out of date after this change:
  - it now names the timeline fragment among the masked responses (it used to say "three HTML fields of /state");
  - it now says the fragment reads the shared timeline cache, not the 5-second page cache.
- **Tidied.** The `render-task-page.js` entry in `docs/architecture/source-map.md` now names the new section and its desktop grid area.
- **Noted, under `## Lessons`:**
  - `docs/areas/front-end-pages.md`: the guest spend strip with its three-response gate, and that the desktop grid needs a `grid-area` for each new section.
  - `docs/areas/front-end-browser.md`: a page script's second request keeps the poll's discipline, and the task-page CSS guards.
- **For close-out.** A single-flight TTL cache is now written a fourth time:
  - `lib/task-timeline.js` `createTimelineFragmentReader` (this change);
  - `routes/task-share.js` `cachedLoadPage`;
  - `lib/workspace-kpis-cache.js`;
  - `lib/sessions-feed-cache.js`.

  One shared helper would serve all four. It spans the web-routes and runs-and-dispatch areas.
- **For close-out.** The task page now reads a task's sessions twice: Stages from loops, and the timeline from the cost read, joined by item id to decide "running". One session model for both was named in the survey as not this task's.
- **For close-out.** `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md` is at 6,143 of its 6,144 bytes, so this change's runs-and-dispatch lesson could not land there. That lesson: a lane is "running" from the page's open ids, not the cost row; and per-lineage `incomplete`, not `lineagesTruncated`, decides "not complete". The note needs trimming first.
- **Waiting entries settled by this change:** none.

## Review — LIN-4405

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2390, head `719bc9e622f910dce4dfc658516ddccf2a85579c` (base `9cf51ef72`; main has moved 5 commits since, none touching this PR's files; MERGEABLE).

CI: green on `719bc9e62`. `ci-success`, Unit tests, all four E2E shards and the source secret scan pass. I also re-ran the four new unit files plus run-evidence, key-state-roundtrip/census and area-map-placement locally (91/91), and ran `tests/e2e/task-timeline.spec.js` locally (3/3).

### How the work meets what was asked
- **Done when / the picture.** A new section, "Sessions on one clock", sits under Stages (`lib/render-task-page.js`, `lib/render-task-timeline.js`). Each lane shows kind (held / fresh / by kind), model, elapsed vs worked time and cost. It also shows wake and resume ticks, a merge mark or "merged, time not recorded", outlines for old lineages and clipped foreign lanes. **Met.**
- **Ruled narrowing (guests have no dollars).** The guest page and `/t/:token/timeline` go through `withoutSpend`, a copy, and `/state` carries no timeline. **Met.** The mutations below confirm it.
- **session-roles.** Precedence is wake → resumed → orchestration → work, and `ORCHESTRATION_KINDS` is imported, not copied. Builder note 6 (a plain `custom` base reads by its kind) is met. Stages' `groupSessions` is untouched (Departure 1). **Met.**
- **task-timeline.** The function is pure, and `withoutSpend` copies (builder note 5). The reader composes `readTaskCost` with `foundedElsewhere: true` and takes the loader's close-out events instead of reading them again. **Met.**
  - "Running" comes from the page's open ids, not the worker row. A missing end reads "end not recorded". Working segments have a minimum width, and a dispatch with no records gets a tick, not a bar.
  - Breaks fold at 10 min / 15 %. A foreign lane uses only its tagged dispatches and is clipped. The merge rule de-duplicates by `prUrl`, then falls back to `pr.mergedAt` on page load only.
- **Truncation reads "not complete".** This was changed under the As-asked block's own authority ("where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so") and posted on LIN-4395 (`d61b450d` §2). I checked the claim in code. A lineage with a missing member that could change its figure is `incomplete` (`task-cost-read.js:405`). Any incomplete lineage nulls `totalUsd` (`cost-read.js:697-702`), so the total still reads "not complete" whenever truncation can change it. The shared flag still shows a note. **Met, by the recorded course change.**
- **run-evidence `pr.mergedAt`.** Additive. **Met.**
- **Renderer.** Positioned HTML with no SVG. Labels sit above the track below 600px and in a label column on desktop. Each lane is a `<details>` with a named `<summary>`. Dollars only go through `formatUsd`, and no cost appears in any attribute. **Met.**
- **Loader.** `loadTaskPage` sets `model.timeline`. `loadTaskState` does not call the reader. A failed read renders "sessions could not be read" and the page still loads. **Met.**
- **Routes.** Both fragments exist. Owner/member uses the same `workspaceFromUrl` middleware as `/state`. The guest route goes `resolveScopedRecord` → cache → `withoutSpend` → `maskFragment`. **Met.** The cache departure (a shared 30s single-flight cache instead of `cachedLoadPage`) is justified by the survey's finding that a 5s TTL can never serve a 60s poll. It is posted on LIN-4395 and registered in the per-key reset.
- **Client.** A coalesced refresher fetches at most once per 60s. It pauses on a hidden tab and stops on 401/404. The `:71` comment is updated (builder note 8). **Met**, with one gap (fix 1 below).
- **Docs.** `areas.json` (session-roles, task-timeline), `source-map.md` and the `llms.txt` `data-*` entries are updated. **Met.**
- **Untouched.** Live Console, `timeline-zoom.js`, the run-page step model and `pipeline-churn` do not appear in the diff. **Met.**

### Regression check
`git log -30` on each touched file shows no fix being undone or revert being re-applied. Main's recent public/ rules still hold:
- LIN-4304: DOM access uses `querySelector`.
- LIN-4292: it covered only the four DOM methods; the `typeof window.initLocalTimes` guard matches the file's existing spelling.

`fa4bb76fb` (Part 1) is intact.

### Mutation checks (LIN-2274)
13 mutations, each reverted afterwards (tree clean). 12 turned their tests red:
- `withoutSpend` keeps a dispatch's `costUsd`, or mutates its input (no clone)
- the guest fragment or guest page skips `withoutSpend`
- "running" is never detected
- a foreign lane's lineage start stretches the clock
- no break folds
- an unknown span may fold
- the `pr.mergedAt` fallback is removed
- held is set without wakes
- the client does not stop on done
- the loader drops the timeline

**Stayed green:** removing the renderer's own `if (!spend) return null` gate in `laneCost`. No dollar leaks, because `withoutSpend` has already removed the figures, but the guest would then read "not priced" / "cost not complete" / "no usage posted" per lane. Fix 2 below.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
- **"A guest response strips money from the model."** Isolated: this is the first money on the task page (the survey confirmed `render-task-page.js` had no `formatUsd`), and `/state` carries no timeline.
- **"A kind→role map."** It has a sibling: the stale private `ORCHESTRATION_KINDS` in `lib/pipeline-churn.js:55`, which lacks `periodical`. It is **outside**: this deliverable doesn't depend on it, and the plan put `pipeline-churn` out of scope. It is a follow-up for close-out, if one is not already filed.

### Leftovers (each has one home)
- **Single-flight TTL cache, now written four times** (`createTimelineFragmentReader`, `cachedLoadPage`, `workspace-kpis-cache`, `sessions-feed-cache`). It spans web-routes and runs-and-dispatch, so it is **outside**: close-out files a follow-up.
- **One session model for Stages and the timeline.** The survey named it as not this task's, so it is **outside**: close-out files a follow-up.
- **runs-and-dispatch lesson.** It is inside the area and fix-sized, so close-out lands it on the PR branch (fix 3).

### Fixes for close-out to make on the PR branch
1. **`public/task-page.js`, `apply(state)` (around line 825): the done edge swallows the last timeline change.** When the poll first reports `status === 'done'`, `timeline.stop()` runs without a final fetch. That same poll is usually the one whose `trackHtml` changed because the last session ended, so the section can keep a lane painted "running … so far" with a now-line until reload. The close-out press reloads via `doneNow`, but other paths to done do not.
   - **Fix:** give `createTimelineRefresher` a `finish()` that, unless already stopped, fetches once immediately (ignoring the window), applies the result, then stops. In `apply`, call `timeline.finish()` on the first `done` instead of `stop()`.
   - **Test:** add one in `tests/unit/task-timeline-client.test.js` that a `done` state after a changed track produces exactly one fetch and no timer.
2. **`tests/unit/task-timeline-page.test.js` (renderer/guest block): pin the renderer's own spend gate.** Assert that `renderTaskTimeline(withoutSpend(t))`, for a timeline with a priced lane, an incomplete lane, a no-telemetry lane and a foreign lane, contains none of `not priced`, `cost not complete`, `no usage posted`, `lineage cost`, `total`. Check it goes red with the `if (!spend) return null;` line in `laneCost` removed.
3. **`docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`: trim, then add the lesson.** The file is 6,143 of 6,144 bytes. Trim an existing entry first, then add under `## Lessons`: "- A task timeline lane is running from the page's open session ids (`isOpenState`), never from the cost row; and a lineage's own `incomplete`, not the shared `lineagesTruncated`, decides "not complete" (LIN-4405, `lib/task-timeline.js`)." Keep the file ≤ 6,144 bytes.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside: the real production picture for LIN-4393.** The fixture is captured data run through unit tests, not the live page. **After the deploy:** open `/workspace/<key>/task/LIN-4393` as owner and confirm:
  - 8 lanes
  - an autopilot lane reading held, elapsed ≈ 63m, worked 2m 22s, with 5 wake ticks
  - the build lane with 2 segments and a resume tick
  - a merge mark

  Also open one task last dispatched more than 7 days ago and confirm its lanes are outlines marked "working times unknown".
- **Inside: guest has no dollars against live data.** Unit-tested with seeded data only. **After the deploy:** mint a share link for a priced task and fetch `/t/<token>`, `/t/<token>/timeline` and `/t/<token>/state`. Confirm no `$` and no cost attribute (`grep -c '\$'` = 0 in the section, the fragment and state).
- **Inside: GitHub's real `merged_at` contract.** `pr.mergedAt` is tested against a stub. **After the deploy:** open a merged task whose close-out events predate `prMergedAt` (pre-LIN-3713). The page load should show the merge mark at GitHub's merge time, not "time not recorded".
- **Inside: page-load cost on large tasks.** Every owner page load (`no-store`) and every guest page-cache miss now does a whole-life cost read, including request records. CI has no realistic data volume. **After the deploy:** load the task page for the largest recent parent (e.g. LIN-4395) and compare its server time with a task without the section. Look for the `Task page timeline read failed` log.
  - **Named monitor:** that `console.error` line, which fires on a failed read. A slow-but-successful read only shows up in production timings.
- **Inside: real phones and other browsers.** The e2e test checks 390px in Chromium only. **Before the merge, or after the deploy by a human:** open a task on an actual phone (iOS Safari). Confirm labels sit above tracks, there is no horizontal scroll, and a lane's `<details>` opens.
- **Rollback:** revert PR #2390's merge commit. The change is additive: no migration and no persisted new shape, and `pr.mergedAt` is a read-only field. It is reversible.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

## Close-out — LIN-4405
